summary: This class explains the traditional custom of Qirayat, where Hahamim were hired to read the Zohar or Tehillim in the house of mourners during the Shiva period to elevate the soul of the deceased. It details how these daily readings concluded at the end of the week with Divre Torah and meals, and how the practice has evolved over time.
questions: What is the meaning of Qirayat in the context of mourning?
Why were Hahamim hired to read in the house of mourners?
What texts were traditionally read during the Shiva period?
How did the practice of Qirayat conclude at the end of the week?
Why did the custom shift from reading the Zohar to reading Tehillim?
